  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B has sourced, priced competitors in the same category. Foray charges $60 per blueprint or $299/mo, MarketGeist $49/mo, Insightloop $99/mo and Gixo $10/mo per workspace. A's direct competitors (Foundry, People.Build, Nixbly, buildapart.io) are all free and pre-revenue, and its only priced comparable, CoFoundersLab at $29/mo, sits in the adjacent co-founder-matching space.",
    "A's concept is not defined. The brief itself says 'one-line description to confirm' and lists the customer as 'varies by idea'. Without a fixed product or payer, a 90-day path to a paying customer is hard to plan. B states a concrete product and a hypothesized payer: operators, consultants and product leaders.",
    "A's demand evidence works against it. The same thread that supplies the single 'looking for someone to make apps' post also contains the rebuttal that 'you can just vibe code if you have an idea'. The brief itself says AI tools are eroding A's core need.",
    "A's competitors show no real traction, and some display labelled dummy data. That points to a commodity format with weak demand. B's niche is also crowded, but paid tiers are visible there, which suggests buyers exist and a solo builder could take share with a sharper wedge.",
    "Both ideas look buildable in six weeks by one person with agents. B's brief cites existing small-team agentic pipelines (Foray, Gixo) as evidence. A's buildability argument rests only on competitors being thin landing pages, which also hints that the format is not worth much."

  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence is one Reddit post, reached through a third-party mirror snapshot rather than the original thread. The same thread directly rebuts the premise ('there is no such thing as an \"ideas guy\" anymore'). Nothing shows anyone paying, or saying they would pay, to have a friend or community builder make a prototype.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. B is clearly better on payer and competitor-pricing evidence, but it has real weaknesses. Its demand quotes describe general decision paralysis, not demand for a tool, and one says 'Only you can' choose, which cuts against the premise. PREONZ pricing is NOT FOUND. The ~$104 cost per lead sits badly against a $60 one-off price. Users may simply default to a general-purpose LLM. B wins mainly because A's evidence is weaker and its concept is undefined, not because B's case is strong."
